# Ben Android Builds

Each row is a debug-signed APK produced by `./scripts/bootstrap.sh` or
`./gradlew assembleDebug` and copied here. Filename convention:

```
Ben-<versionName>-<gitShortSHA>[-dirty]-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.apk
```

The actual `.apk` files are gitignored (they're ~85 MB each); only this
changelog ships in the repo.

| Filename | Date | Version | Commit | Highlights |

| `Ben-0.1.9-7c255a7-dirty-20260514-1040.apk` | 2026-05-14 10:40 | 0.1.9 | `7c255a7` (dirty) | **Two Android-platform-specific blockers fixed after the 0.1.8 diagnostic stream pinpointed them on a real Samsung S24.** The 0.1.8 logs showed `[VOICE/TOOLS_FETCH] FAILED after 3 attempts: NetworkOnMainThreadException` followed by `tools=0 facts=false` followed by 11 turns of "I'm here to help" / "Sure, just let me know" / "Opening WhatsApp" lies with zero tool calls. Two distinct bugs - one root cause for "Ben can't act on the device", one for "Ben keeps talking after I say Ben". (1) **`connect()` runs off-main now** (`BenVoiceService.kt`). Pre-fix `onStartCommand` called `connect()` directly and `connect()` opened sockets to the embedded Node bridge (`fetchToolsFromBridge` on port 18791, `fetchSessionContextFromBridge` on the same port). Android forbids socket I/O on the main thread - all 3 retry attempts in 0.1.8 immediately threw `NetworkOnMainThreadException`, were caught by my Exception handler, and `sessionTools` ended up `[]`. The model was shipped `tools: []` in `session.update` and literally had no function-calling vocabulary - it could only chat. Fix: new dedicated `bootstrapExecutor` (`Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor` named `ben-voice-bootstrap`); `onStartCommand` now does `bootstrapExecutor.execute { connect() }`. New `BOOTSTRAP_THREAD` diagnostic event emitted at the top of `connect()` so MicTest will show the thread name (must be `ben-voice-bootstrap`, never `main`). bootstrapExecutor is shut down in `stopAndRearm()` alongside `toolExecutor`. (2) **Mic mute now waits for the AudioTrack to drain** (`BenVoiceService.kt` + `OpenAiConfig.MIC_MUTE_TAIL_MS`). Pre-fix `isAssistantSpeaking` flipped to false on `response.done` - but `response.done` fires when the model marks the response complete server-side, NOT when AudioTrack finishes draining the buffered tail audio (typically 200-800ms more). During that window the mic gate was open, the speaker was still playing the model's tail words, the mic captured the speaker bleed, whisper transcribed it as new "user" input, my `shouldRespondTo` filter accepted it (because it didn't look like a wake-only or noise transcript), and we drove a new `response.create`. Infinite chatter loop. Empirically the canonical case from 0.1.8 logs was the model saying "Opening WhatsApp" -> whisper hearing "Binning WhatsApp" 2.5s later -> model responding "Sure" -> bleed continues. Fix: new `bytesWrittenToAudioTrack: Long` counter incremented on every `audioTrack.write()` return value, new `drainPollRunnable` posted on `mainHandler` after `response.done` that polls every 50ms comparing `audioTrack.playbackHeadPosition` (in frames) against `bytesWrittenToAudioTrack / 2` (PCM16-mono frame count) and only flips `isAssistantSpeaking=false` when the playback head catches the write head. Hard fallback at `OpenAiConfig.MIC_MUTE_TAIL_MS=1200` for devices where playbackHeadPosition returns 0 / negative or AudioTrack is null. New `MIC_UNMUTE` diagnostic event emits with `drained head=X/Y` (perfect drain) or `fallback_timeout head=X/Y` (had to use the timer). audio.delta handler now cancels any pending drain poll because more audio means the drain window restarts after the LAST delta. (3) **Echo-similarity transcript guard** (`BenVoiceService.shouldRespondTo` + `textSimilarity`). Defense-in-depth for the cases where AEC / mute-gate still leak. New `lastAssistantTranscript: String` field captured on `response.audio_transcript.done` (truncated to 200 chars). `shouldRespondTo()` now runs a Damerau-Levenshtein-based similarity ratio between the cleaned new transcript and the cleaned last assistant transcript - if >= 0.7 the transcript is treated as echo and the response.create is skipped. Quick-reject if length-difference > 50% (don't even start the DP table). New `TRANSCRIPT_SKIP echo XX%:'...'` diagnostic event so the user can see the echo guard firing. Catches "Opening WhatsApp" -> "Binning WhatsApp" because they're 1 character apart in tokenized form (~92% similarity). (4) **Hard refusal when tools fail to load** (`BenVoiceService.connect()` + new `speakRefusalAndEnd`). Pre-fix when `sessionTools.length()==0` we just shipped `tools:[]` to OpenAI and let the model monologue helplessly. Now: emit `SESSION_REFUSED no_tools`, then open a minimal Realtime WSS that pushes a single `conversation.item.create` (input_text: "Read this sentence aloud verbatim, then stop: <message>") + `response.create`, plays back the audio, and tears down on `response.done` with a `MIC_MUTE_TAIL_MS` drain delay. The user hears one honest sentence ("My device tools didn't load this time. Please try again in a moment.") instead of either silence or 5 minutes of lies. Wake listener resumes cleanly. (5) **`RESPONSE_CANCELLED` event** for `status=cancelled` responses (caused by our own `response.cancel` from stop-intent or echo guard) - keeps MicTest log readable; previously these surfaced as `RESPONSE_DONE status=cancelled output=0[]` which looked like a bug. (6) **History writer ack diagnostic** (`VoiceNodeBridgeNotifier.kt`). Pre-fix the user reported "history not being saved" with no way to tell whether the Node bridge was reachable. Two changes: (a) new `sendWithAck()` variant with an `(ok, errMsg) -> Unit` callback; `notifySessionStarted` uses it and emits `HISTORY_WRITE_OK session.started recorded` or `HISTORY_WRITE_FAILED session.started failed: ...` to MicTest. (b) bumped `Socket.soTimeout` from 250ms to 800ms because right after wake the embedded Node bridge can still be flushing boot tasks - 250ms was empirically not enough to catch the response back even when the writer was successful, so we logged failure and surfaced it to the user as broken history. (7) **Version bump** 0.1.8 -> 0.1.9 (`versionCode` 9 -> 10). **Why these were Android-only**: Mac CoreAudio routes loopback through a separate audio unit (no speaker bleed), Cocoa allows network on the main thread (no NetworkOnMainThreadException), and Mac omniclaw is one always-running Node process (no Service lifecycle / Looper / FGS-type ceremony). 90% of what we've been chasing is pure Android-platform quirks. Build size 89 MB, same 3 ABIs as 0.1.8. |
| `Ben-0.1.7-7c255a7-dirty-20260513-1600.apk` | 2026-05-13 16:00 | 0.1.7 | `7c255a7` (dirty) | **Real-device follow-up on 0.1.6 user reports: "WhatsApp giving fake location", "not opening WhatsApp", "still blabbering when I don't speak", "fix worked a little bit but still has errors". The 0.1.6 auto-greet fix was wrong: my `userHasSpokenThisSession` flag flipped to true the moment whisper transcribed the wake phrase audio ("hey ban") inside the WSS, so by the time the auto-greet `response.created` fired the guard was already disarmed. This build replaces that approach with a bulletproof server-side fix.** (1) **Auto-greet eliminated at the source** (`BenVoiceService.kt` + `OpenAiConfig.kt`). Set `turn_detection.create_response: false` in the Realtime `session.update`. The server now NEVER auto-starts a response. We manually call `response.create` only when `conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed` arrives with a transcript that passes a new `shouldRespondTo()` gate. The gate rejects: empty/whitespace transcripts; transcripts under 4 chars (except "yes"/"no"/"ok"); whisper's well-known noise phrases ("", ".", "...", "thank you", "you", "uh", "um", "hmm", "mm", "ah", "oh", "yeah", "ya" - whisper emits one of these for almost any audio buffer that's just room hum / breath / fan noise); transcripts that strip to the wake phrase only after dropping a leading preamble token ("ok", "okay", "hey", "yo", "uh", "um", "hello", "hi") and the wake word matched via `WakePhraseMatcher.matches`. Stop intents are still detected and end the session. The auto-greet fundamentally cannot happen now because the server is never permitted to start a response unprompted. Removed the v0.1.6 cancel-after-the-fact path and the `userHasSpokenThisSession` flag (replaced with a `userTurnsAnswered` counter used only for diagnostics). (2) **Fresh location fix** (`AndroidDeviceBridge.getLocation`). Pre-fix the tool returned whatever `getLastKnownLocation()` had cached - on Samsung this is often a stale fix from another app from minutes/hours ago, which the model then reverse-geocoded into a confidently-wrong "you're in Bengaluru". Fix: new `requestFreshLocation(lm, preferGps, timeoutMs=4_000)` helper requests a single update from each available provider (GPS / FUSED / NETWORK) in parallel, awaits the first arrival on a CountDownLatch with a 4 s ceiling, and removes the listeners cleanly. If fresh fails we fall back to last-known and mark the result `freshness="last_known"` + `is_stale=true` when age > 5 min. New system prompt clause **LOCATION HONESTY RULE**: "When device.get_location returns is_stale=true or freshness=last_known with age_ms > 5 minutes, you MUST tell the user the location is approximate / from your last known fix and mention the age in plain words. Never speak a stale location as if it were current. Never describe a location you have not actually called device.get_location for - if you only have user-stated home address from USER FACTS, say 'Your saved home is X, but I don't have a fresh GPS fix right now.' Do not silently substitute USER FACTS for live location." Uses `LocationManager` directly (no Play Services dep) so it works on non-GMS ROMs too. (3) **Fuzzier `ui.click` text matching** (`assets/node/src/openclaw/builtin_tools.js`). Pre-fix the click-by-text path did a single case-insensitive substring match on `node.text/contentDescription/label`. On real WhatsApp's Chats list each row's text is the full contact name ("Pragati Biradar") OR a compound "Name • Last message preview" string - a substring match on "Pragati" worked but on "Pragati B" did NOT, and substring also misses diacritics ("Björn" vs "Bjorn"). Fix: 3-tier matching - tier 1 exact case-insensitive substring; tier 2 token-prefix (any whitespace-separated token starts with the query, or the joined-tokens-string starts with the query, so "Pragati B" matches "Pragati Biradar"); tier 3 NFD-normalized diacritic-stripped substring. Matches are ranked by tier ASC, then `clickable=true` first, then doc order. Error messages now spell out which tiers we tried so the model can give the user actionable feedback. (4) **In-app diagnostic stream** (`BenVoiceService.kt` + `MicTestActivity.kt`). New `BenVoiceService.ACTION_VOICE_EVENT` LocalBroadcast + 120-event ring buffer (`voiceEventBuffer`) emitting `SESSION_START` / `WSS_OPEN` / `TRANSCRIPT` / `TRANSCRIPT_SKIP` / `STOP_INTENT` / `RESPONSE_CREATE` / `TOOL_CALL` / `TOOL_RESULT` / `WSS_FAILURE` / `WSS_CLOSED` / `SESSION_END`. MicTestActivity now registers receivers for BOTH the wake events (`WAKE/...`) and voice events (`VOICE/...`), merges them by timestamp, and clears both buffers on the Clear button. The user can now screenshot a single MicTest log that shows the entire flow: wake match -> WSS open -> what whisper heard -> whether we skipped the transcript and why -> which tools the model called -> what each tool returned (first 120 chars) -> when the session ended. No adb required. (5) **Version bump** 0.1.6 -> 0.1.7 (`versionCode` 7 -> 8). **What's still NOT fixed (waiting on diagnostics from the MicTest log in this build)**: the actual WhatsApp flow failure mode - was it not opening at all, or opening but the model never called the tools, or calling tools and getting an error? With the auto-greet fix the model should now actually run the tool sequence instead of monologuing, and with the diagnostic stream the user can show me which step failed. Build size 85 MB, same 3 ABIs as 0.1.6. |
| `Ben-0.1.6-7c255a7-dirty-20260513-1450.apk` | 2026-05-13 14:50 | 0.1.6 | `7c255a7` (dirty) | **Real-device fixes after 0.1.5 was installed on a Samsung One UI 6 phone (`en-IN` locale). User-reported failures: wake recognizer stuck in `ERROR_LANGUAGE_UNAVAILABLE (code=13)` loop; model auto-greeting "I can help you" before any user utterance; `device.get_location` returning useless raw lat/lon; "Check offline language pack" button landing on Samsung's wrong "Digital assistant app" screen; WhatsApp UI automation racing the app's launch animation.** (1) **Wake-word locale fallback rewritten** (`BenWakewordService.kt`). Pre-fix the recognizer hard-pinned `EXTRA_LANGUAGE="en-US"` AND set `EXTRA_ONLY_RETURN_LANGUAGE_PREFERENCE=true`, so on a Samsung phone whose on-device pack was only `en-IN` every request hard-failed with code 13. The "fall back to network recognizer" path from 0.1.3 was useless because it still asked for the same `en-US` and we never actually switched recognizer instances. Fix: drop the strict-preference flag, walk a candidate locale list `[en-US, en-IN, en-GB, system-default, no-locale]` on each `ERROR_LANGUAGE_UNAVAILABLE` / `ERROR_LANGUAGE_NOT_SUPPORTED`, AND force-switch from `createOnDeviceSpeechRecognizer` to `createSpeechRecognizer` (network) when the on-device list exhausts. `ACTION_FORCE_RESTART` now resets the locale index + recognizer-type to clean state. Per-restart log lines now say `starting recognizer=on-device|network locale='en-IN' preferOffline=true` so MicTest immediately shows whether the fallback engaged. (2) **Auto-greeting suppression** (`BenVoiceService.kt` + `OpenAiConfig.kt`). On the real device the model fired a `response.created` and started saying "How can I help you?" / "I can help you" before the user had said anything. Two reasons: (a) `VAD_THRESHOLD=0.6` was sensitive enough to misclassify ambient room noise / our own first audio frames as user speech, and (b) gpt-realtime sometimes emits a spontaneous greeting on session open even with explicit "do not greet" instructions. Fix: bumped VAD threshold to 0.8 and prefix_padding to 500ms (`OpenAiConfig`); added a `userHasSpokenThisSession` flag in `BenVoiceService` that flips to true only on the first `conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed` with ≥2 chars of real transcript; while it's false, any incoming `response.created` is immediately killed with `response.cancel` (auto-greet guard). System prompt now has a dedicated SILENCE-ON-OPEN RULE clause: "At session start you receive NO user input. DO NOT produce any audio, text, greeting, filler, or status message of any kind unless and until you have received a clearly-directed user utterance" and an UNCLEAR-INPUT RULE clause covering ambient noise / echo. (3) **Reverse-geocoding in `device.get_location`** (`AndroidDeviceBridge.kt`). Pre-fix the tool returned raw `{latitude, longitude, accuracy_m, source, age_ms}` and the model said "I have coordinates 12.97, 77.59" because the prompt's WEATHER flow reverse-geocodes via wttr.in but pure location queries had nothing. Fix: after the fix is obtained, run `Geocoder(ctx).getFromLocation(lat, lon, 1)` (legacy sync API, fine because we're already off-main-thread) and enrich the result with `city`, `district`, `state`, `country`, `country_code`, `postal_code`, `full_address`, `place` (joined), and `summary` (the one-sentence string the model should speak verbatim - `"Bengaluru, India"` / `"Whitefield, Bengaluru"`). Wrapped in try/catch because Geocoder fails offline; the lat/lon path is preserved as the floor. (4) **Samsung-aware "Check offline language pack" button** (`OnboardingActivity.kt`). Pre-fix the canonical `Settings.ACTION_VOICE_INPUT_SETTINGS` intent on Samsung One UI 6 redirects to "Digital assistant app" (unrelated). Fix: new `openVoiceInputSettings()` helper with a fallback chain - on Samsung the canonical intent is skipped, then try Google app launch intent (`com.google.android.googlequicksearchbox`), then Speech Services by Google app info (`com.google.android.tts`), then the canonical intent as last resort, then generic Settings. When we fall back, the user gets a short Toast explaining what to look for ("Open this app -> Offline speech recognition -> download English"). On Pixel / OnePlus / OnePlus / stock Android the canonical intent still fires first and works as before. (5) **App-launch settle delay** (`AndroidDeviceBridge.launchApp` + `BenAccessibilityService.launchApp`). Pre-fix `device.launch_app` returned `ok` the instant `startActivity()` was called, which raced the app's first frame. The model's immediately-next `ui.read_screen` call hit the launcher or a half-painted launch animation, decided "nothing matches", and gave up. Fix: 700ms `Thread.sleep` before returning ok (we're already off-main-thread on the Node-bridge executor, so this doesn't ANR), and the result now includes `settle_ms: 700` so the harness can see the delay was applied. This is enough for warm-launches of WhatsApp / Swiggy / Settings on a mid-range device; cold-launches still need a second `ui.read_screen` and the existing accessibility-not-bound fallback. (6) **Version bump** 0.1.5 -> 0.1.6 (`versionCode` 6 -> 7). **Validation**: Kotlin `compileDebugKotlin` clean (only pre-existing deprecation warnings on legacy contacts API and `LocalBroadcastManager`), `assembleDebug` clean for all three ABIs, JS test suite all green (`automation_simulation` 8/8, `kotlin_rpc` 10/10, `tools_rpc` 11 tools, `wake_phrase_matcher` 38/38). APK contents verified by strings dump: `userHasSpokenThisSession`, `candidateLocales`, `auto-greet guard disarmed`, `exhausted locales on on-device recognizer -> switching to NETWORK recognizer`, `Geocoder` import, `openVoiceInputSettings`, `com.google.android.googlequicksearchbox`, `com.google.android.tts`, `SILENCE-ON-OPEN RULE`, `reverse-geocode failed` are all present in the dex chunks. **What is still NOT fixed (needs your logcat to diagnose)**: WhatsApp UI automation failing past the launch step (the settle delay above is one likely cause but not the only one - real WhatsApp on Compose may need vision.locate_text fallback; need `adb logcat -s BenAccessibilityService BenVoiceService` from a failing run to know what tree/click error actually fires). Build size 85 MB. |

| `Ben-0.1.5-7c255a7-dirty-20260512-1152.apk` | 2026-05-12 11:52 | 0.1.5 | `7c255a7` (dirty) | **Bundle of 12 fixes from `android/DIAGNOSIS.md` plus FUTURE_WORK #2 (S3 sensitivity hard-refusal). Single-session execution of every "Smallest patch" the diagnosis pass identified, validated against real OpenAI endpoints + the existing JS test suite + a 12-scenario USE_CASES.md trace.** (1) **Accessibility config no longer bricks the device** — `accessibility_service_config.xml` drops `flagRequestTouchExplorationMode` (which forced TalkBack-style touch interception, breaking all normal taps the moment Ben's accessibility service was enabled) and removes `packageNames="@null"` (which on Samsung One UI 6+ resolved to an empty array and silently starved the service of events). (2) **Onboarding step 0 now requests RECORD_AUDIO + POST_NOTIFICATIONS + CAMERA at runtime** via a new "Allow microphone, notifications & camera" button + button label that flips to "...granted ✓" once accepted. Pre-fix the wake-word service silently failed on first boot because `RECORD_AUDIO` was declared but never granted. Step 0 also gains an OEM-specific autostart deep-link button — `Build.MANUFACTURER` / `Build.BRAND` detection routes Xiaomi/Redmi/Poco to `com.miui.securitycenter/.permcenter.autostart.AutoStartManagementActivity`, Oppo/Realme to `com.coloros.safecenter/.permission.startup.StartupAppListActivity`, Vivo to `com.iqoo.secure/.AddWhiteListActivity`, Huawei/Honor to `com.huawei.systemmanager/.startupmgr.ui.StartupNormalAppListActivity`, OnePlus to `com.oneplus.security/.chainlaunch.view.ChainLaunchAppListActivity`, with Samsung falling through to app-info and unknown vendors to the generic battery panel. Each tries up to 2 candidate ComponentNames and falls through gracefully. (3) **Foreground service `startForeground` Android 14+ compliance** — `BenForegroundService` now calls the 3-arg `startForeground(id, notif, FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_MICROPHONE \| FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_SPECIAL_USE)` on Q+ (API 29+); pre-fix on `targetSdk=35` Android 14+ would throw `MissingForegroundServiceTypeException` because the manifest declared `foregroundServiceType` but the service used the deprecated 2-arg overload. Same fix applied to `BenScreencapService` with `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_MEDIA_PROJECTION`. Defensive fallback retries with MICROPHONE-only on OEM ROMs that reject SPECIAL_USE. (4) **`ben://pair` activity-alias** — `AndroidManifest` now lists both `ben://pair` (canonical) and `jarvis://pair` (legacy) inside the `PairingDeepLink` filter; `PairingActivity.parsePairingUri` and `isPairingUri` accept either scheme; `pairing_paste_invalid` toast updated to mention both. (5) **Pairing handshake actually verifies** — `PairingActivity.handleScanned` no longer toasts "Paired with Mac" unconditionally; it kicks `peer.pair_now`, waits 1.5 s for the WSS handshake, then polls a NEW `peer.pair_status` RPC handler (added to `assets/node/src/bridge/inbound_rpc.js`) for up to 5 s. The handler does an active `peer.ping` against the live client and returns `{paired: bool, last_error?}`. On miss the user gets the new `pairing_status_unverified` warning with a clear "Mac may be offline / on a different network / running an older daemon" message instead of a false-positive success. (6) **Cross-device delegation surfaces a useful error instead of `unknown_method`** — `peer.delegate` in `assets/node/src/openclaw/builtin_tools.js` now tries `task.run` first (the canonical name from `MIGRATION_TODO.md` item #1) and falls back to legacy `peer.run_task` on `unknown_method`. If both come back unknown, returns `{ok:false, error:"peer_no_task_handler", hint:"The paired Mac does not expose a task-delegation handler. Tell the user their Mac needs the latest omniclaw daemon..."}`. The Realtime model can speak this verbatim. (7) **OpenAI vision fallback chain that ACTUALLY falls back** — `vision.read_screen` in `builtin_tools.js` walks `[gpt-5.5, gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini]` and on each model picks the right token-budget parameter via a NEW `tokenBudgetParam(model)` helper (`max_completion_tokens` for gpt-5* and o-series, `max_tokens` otherwise). Defense-in-depth: if OpenAI returns 400 "Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens'" or "...'max_completion_tokens'" we auto-retry the SAME model with the other param name before walking the chain. **This caught a real bug** during validation in this session — pre-fix the chain treated any 4xx as fatal so the very first `gpt-5.5` call (which always 400s with `max_tokens`) short-circuited the entire chain and `gpt-4o` was never even tried. **End-to-end verified against real OpenAI** in this session: all three models in the fallback chain returned "Red" against a 64x64 red test PNG, with `gpt-5.5` correctly auto-switching to `max_completion_tokens`. (8) **Reconnect-with-backoff for Realtime WSS** — `BenVoiceService` now retries up to 3 times with 500/1000/2000 ms backoffs on WSS `onFailure` / unexpected `onClosed`; resets the counter on successful `onOpen`. Pre-fix a single transient handshake failure tore down the session and forced the user to re-wake. (9) **Hardware AEC / NoiseSuppressor / AGC** — `BenVoiceService` attaches `AcousticEchoCanceler.create()`, `NoiseSuppressor.create()`, and `AutomaticGainControl.create()` to the AudioRecord session id when `isAvailable()`. Each in its own try/catch because individual chips lie about isAvailable. Released cleanly in `stopAndRearm()` so we don't leak kernel effect slots. The pre-existing isAssistantSpeaking software gate stays as a backstop for devices without hardware AEC. (10) **Cost ledger subsystem (NEW)** — three new files: `OpenAiConfig.kt` (single-source-of-truth for every OpenAI constant — endpoint, model, voice, language, sample rate, VAD, timers, reconnect attempts/backoffs, vision fallback chain, cost prices, default daily/monthly caps), `CostLedger.kt` (singleton that records token usage per `CallKind` bucket — REALTIME_AUDIO, REALTIME_TEXT, VISION, CHAT — with daily/monthly running totals persisted to `BenSecrets` as micro-USD Long, automatic date/month rollover, RefusalReason enum + AtomicReference for hard-cap refusal). `BenSecrets` gains 6 new keys (`cost_daily_usd_micro`, `cost_daily_date`, `cost_monthly_usd_micro`, `cost_monthly_key`, `cost_daily_cap_usd_micro`, `cost_monthly_cap_usd_micro`) plus `dailyCapUsd()` / `monthlyCapUsd()` accessors with default fallbacks. `BenVoiceService.connect()` now does `CostLedger.checkRefusal(ctx)` BEFORE opening the WSS — caps stop the session at session-start, not after another 30 s of audio. `recordCostFromResponseDone(ev)` extracts `usage.input_tokens` / `output_tokens` from each `response.done` and feeds it through `CostLedger.record(REALTIME_AUDIO, ...)`. (11) **S3 sensitivity hard refusal (FUTURE_WORK #2)** — `BenAccessibilityService.typeText` checks `target.isPassword` before issuing `ACTION_SET_TEXT`. UPI PIN, banking PIN, screen-unlock, password-manager, and any `EditText` with `inputType=textPassword` / `numberPassword` / `textVisiblePassword` is refused with `{ok:false, error:"password_field_refused", hint:"This is a password / PIN field. I cannot type into it for safety reasons - please enter it yourself."}`.
